pharm: Non-cardioselective beta-adrenoceptor blocking agent applied topically to the eye to reduce intraocular pressure by decreasing aqueous humor production.
quick: One to two drops of 0.5% solution in affected eye(s) once daily; severe cases twice daily (0.25% also available)
Topical ophthalmic; not related to meals
Use only if benefit justifies risk; systemic beta-blockade possible
Beta-blockers may pass into milk; use caution
No specific ocular dose adjustment; systemic absorption is low
No specific interaction with eye drops
Intraocular pressure, heart rate, signs of bronchospasm/systemic beta-blockade
summary: Levobunolol is a non-cardioselective topical ophthalmic beta-adrenergic blocking agent used to lower elevated intraocular pressure in chronic open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension. It reduces aqueous humor production without significantly affecting pupil size or accommodation. The usual dose is one to two drops of the 0.5% solution in the affected eye(s) once daily, increasing to twice daily for more severe or inadequately controlled cases; a 0.25% strength is also available. Intraocular pressure reduction begins within about 1 hour, peaks at 2-6 hours, and can last up to 24 hours. Because enough drug can be absorbed systemically to cause beta-blockade, it is contraindicated in patients with bronchial asthma, severe COPD, sinus bradycardia, second- or third-degree AV block, overt cardiac failure, and cardiogenic shock.
indications: Lowering of elevated intraocular pressure in chronic open-angle glaucoma
Lowering of elevated intraocular pressure in ocular hypertension

dosage.d: One to two drops in the affected eye(s) once daily; for more severe or uncontrolled pressure, one to two drops twice daily
One to two drops of the 0.25% solution in the affected eye(s) twice daily

admin: Wash hands; tilt head back and instill the drop into the conjunctival sac, avoiding contact of the dropper tip with the eye or any surface
Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner (nasolacrimal occlusion) for 1-2 minutes after instillation to reduce systemic absorption
If more than one topical eye medication is used, separate administration by at least 5 minutes
Remove soft contact lenses before instillation (preservative may be absorbed) and wait before reinserting
Do not touch the dropper tip to prevent contamination; store as directed and protect from light
moa: Levobunolol is a non-selective beta-adrenergic receptor antagonist (blocks both beta-1 and beta-2 receptors) with no significant intrinsic sympathomimetic or membrane-stabilizing activity. Applied topically to the eye, it lowers intraocular pressure primarily by reducing the production of aqueous humor by the ciliary epithelium. Unlike miotics, it does not constrict the pupil or affect accommodation, so it lowers pressure without causing night blindness or accommodative spasm.

absolute: Bronchial asthma or history of bronchial asthma
Overt cardiac failure or cardiogenic shock
Hypersensitivity to levobunolol or any component
relative: Diabetes mellitus or hypoglycemia (may mask warning signs)
Hyperthyroidism (may mask signs; abrupt withdrawal risk)
monitor: Heart rate and signs of bradycardia or heart block
Signs of systemic beta-blockade (hypotension, fatigue, masked hypoglycemia)

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; fetotoxicity was seen in rabbits at high systemic doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Systemically absorbed beta-blockers may affect the fetus/neonate.
lact: Systemic beta-blockers are excreted in human milk, and it is not known whether topical levobunolol reaches milk in clinically significant amounts. Exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman and monitor the infant for signs of beta-blockade (bradycardia).
renal: No specific ophthalmic dosage adjustment is provided for renal impairment; systemic exposure from topical use is low. Monitor for systemic effects in patients with significant comorbidity.
hepatic: No specific ophthalmic dosage adjustment is provided for hepatic impairment; systemic exposure from topical use is low. Monitor for systemic beta-blocker effects.

major: Systemic beta-blockers - additive systemic beta-blockade; use together cautiously
Oral/IV calcium channel blockers (verapamil, diltiazem) - additive AV conduction depression and hypotension
moderate: Catecholamine-depleting drugs (reserpine) - additive hypotension and bradycardia
Antiarrhythmics (e.g., quinidine) and clonidine - conduction and rebound effects
minor: Epinephrine - possible mydriasis when used together topically
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with ophthalmic administration.
interactions.diagnostics: May mask tachycardia/tremor of hypoglycemia and signs of hyperthyroidism; consider when interpreting these in diabetic or thyroid patients.

common: Transient ocular stinging or burning on instillation
serious: Bradycardia, heart block, hypotension, or worsening heart failure
emergency: Severe bradycardia, heart block, or cardiac decompensation

monitoring: Intraocular pressure at baseline and during therapy to confirm response
Heart rate and blood pressure, especially in cardiac patients
Respiratory symptoms in patients with reactive airway disease
Blood glucose awareness in diabetics (beta-blockade can mask hypoglycemia)
Ocular surface for irritation or allergic reaction
counsel: Use the drops exactly as prescribed; press gently on the inner corner of your eye for a minute or two after each drop to limit absorption into the body
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or anything else, to keep it from getting contaminated
Remove contact lenses before using and wait before putting them back in
Tell your doctor if you have asthma, slow heart rate, heart problems, or diabetes - this medicine can affect breathing and heart rate
Report trouble breathing, slow or irregular heartbeat, dizziness, or unusual tiredness
pk: Intraocular pressure reduction detectable within about 1 hour of dosing
Maximum effect between 2 and 6 hours after instillation
Active metabolite (dihydrolevobunolol) contributes to prolonged ocular effect
Intraocular pressure lowering maintained up to 24 hours after a single dose
Store at 15-25 C (59-77 F); protect from light; keep the bottle tightly closed
pearls: Levobunolol IS FDA-approved as an ophthalmic antiglaucoma beta-blocker (do not confuse with non-FDA agents)
Enough drug can be absorbed systemically to cause beta-blockade - the same contraindications as systemic beta-blockers apply (asthma, bradycardia, heart block, heart failure)
Nasolacrimal occlusion (pressing the inner eye corner) after instillation reduces systemic absorption and side effects
Lowers intraocular pressure by reducing aqueous production without affecting pupil size or accommodation - no night blindness like miotics
Can mask the tachycardia and tremor of hypoglycemia in diabetics and signs of hyperthyroidism
missed: If a dose is missed, instill it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular dosing schedule. Do not instill extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Topical overdose is unlikely to cause serious systemic effects, but accidental ingestion or excessive absorption may produce systemic beta-blockade: bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm, and acute heart failure. Treatment is supportive and symptomatic; bradycardia/hypotension may respond to atropine and, if needed, beta-agonists or glucagon. Flush the eye with water if local irritation occurs.
